seal.statement: Every exact checkout the push-gate materializer (scripts/checks/push-gate-corpus-worktree.js --gate) proves a command in - the pre-push gate, the publisher's local corpus and post-merge corpus, the local release proof - is brought to the generated state a CI or lab-placed proof checkout has before the command starts: the sealed import graph (test-output/analysis/global-owner-debt-import-graph.json) generated for that commit by its own producer, through one preparation owner that the lab placement shares. A clean checkout of b3b366573 then runs test/scripts/push-gate-change-proof.test.js green through the materializer, where it ran red (subtests 9, 10, 12, 13: import graph is not generated) in the post-merge corpus. A commit whose generated preparation fails or rewrites tracked metadata is refused, never run without it.

text: Cause and history. test/scripts/push-gate-change-proof.test.js reads the sealed import graph (loadSealedImporters(process.cwd()), scripts/checks/helper-import-closure.js) in sealedImportsOf/gateImportClosure, added by 5f6a779e7 (lean-push-gate, 2026-09-12) and cccf0218e (full-corpus-trigger-gate-definers, 2026-10-03); proof-receipt-bound-to-validated-execution (#187) did not introduce it. The graph test-output/analysis/global-owner-debt-import-graph.json is gitignored and generated by scripts/generate-global-owner-debt-inventory.js --refresh-import-graph-only. Its producers today: CI 'Prepare generated test metadata' (npm run test:metadata:refresh), the lab placement script (scripts/lab/probe.js PLACEMENT_IMPORT_GRAPH), the lab selector (prepareSelectorImportGraph), and the pre-push gate's own test stage (postpush manifest step owner-debt-report-inputs). The materializer push-gate-corpus-worktree.js --gate --run <command> generates nothing, so any command other than the hook - the publisher's local and post-merge corpus, the RELEASE.md local release proof - runs in a checkout without it. The file is a spine test, always in the pushing gate's cone where the hook generated the graph; every earlier local corpus ran only the rest of a cone (e.g. 62d537313: 2127 files, file absent; the 19 recorded .files lists contain it 0 times). b3b366573's post-merge run is the first whole-corpus local run (2551 files) and the first to run it unprepared: red on first pass and retry. Reproduced: push-gate-corpus-worktree.js --gate b3b366573 --run node scripts/run-test-files.js test/scripts/push-gate-change-proof.test.js -> not ok 9, 10, 12, 13 (evidence/red-clean-materialized-b3b366573.log.txt).

Vacuous-green cause behind F1 of the rejection: test/scripts/push-gate-change-proof.test.js gateImportClosure follows TRACKED files only (trackedFiles()), so a lane run while scripts/checks/proof-checkout-preparation.js was still untracked never saw it in the gate's import closure, and subtest 9 stayed green; after commit 49132b8c8 it is tracked, imported by scripts/lab/probe.js which the runner imports, and matched no full-corpus trigger. Rule kept from it: a test that reads tracked files is proven on the committed tree (commit, npm run -s test:metadata:refresh, then run), not on a working tree with new untracked modules.

M2 (recorded, not changed): the publisher's in-place gate path (push-gate-corpus-worktree.js --in-place, used inside the publisher's exact-HEAD worktree) does not call prepareProofCheckout; it runs the pre-push hook, whose test stage generates the graph itself in the postpush manifest step owner-debt-report-inputs before the change proof, so its readers have the graph. Only --gate checkouts running a command other than the hook lacked it. M3 (recorded, not changed): the producer flag --refresh-import-graph-only stays a literal in PROOF_CHECKOUT_GENERATORS, change-selection-constants.js HELPER_IMPORT_GRAPH_HINT, package.json test:metadata:refresh, the postpush manifest JSON and ci.yml. JSON and YAML consumers cannot import a JS constant, and exporting it from the producer for the JS readers would make proof-checkout-preparation.js import scripts/generate-global-owner-debt-inventory.js, pulling the producer's whole import tree into the gate's own import closure, every module of which would then need a full-corpus trigger; one owner per language boundary is the smaller hazard.
